Runtime systems

Gameplay

Gameplay is built from Actors, Components, Constructs, recipes, deployment systems, and services such as economy and match coordination.

Actors

Live world objects with Transform, Components, hierarchy, tags, and lifecycle state.

Components

Live behavior objects. Tag, Resource, and Team definitions can currently be authored; most gameplay Components remain runtime-only or planned.

Resources and Tags

Resources give actors values like Health. Tags describe identity and query groups, but should not replace structured ownership.

Recipes and Constructs

Recipes describe production. Constructs and runtime configurators attach gameplay behavior around spawned roots.

Bases

Bases own match objective behavior, team, account, lane, and production context at runtime.

AI Economy

AI commanders select roster entries, purchase through the economy service, and queue paid deployments.

Architecture Notes

Fragment-authored ownership is a default. Explicit runtime context owns the match. Saved Fragment recipes reuse authored content while runtime systems apply final team, lane, targeting, and combat.
